name: Bishr ibn 'Amr
bio: Bishr ibn 'Amr belonged to the house of Sa'd ibn Malik of Qais ibn Tha'labah, the family of the two Muraqqishes and of Tarafah, and was a kinsman of Maimun al-A'sha. Lyall says little about him is to be gathered from the usual sources.
The Aghani makes him a contemporary of an-Nu'man Abu Qabus.

poems.title: Ode LXX: Say to the Son of Kulthum
poems.author: Bishr ibn 'Amr
poems.note: Lyall's heading: Bishr son of 'Amr, of Qais ibn Tha'labah, of Bakr.
poems.text:
Say to the Son of Kulthum, the stalwart in defence of his own — ' Greet joyfully a War that shall choke the [experienced] old man with his spittle ! '

And [the like] to his two companions : may their morning not be pleasant, when War bares her long fangs for all men to see !

He sends not forth his caravan except after certain proof of the way to glorious deeds : and some folk are scattered hither and thither !

Nay, but seest thou ladies camel-borne, led along in a string, one following another, with some lagging behind, and a driver not outstripped by any ?

They take a side way [between mountains] from the main road, with evenly-coloured [coverings to their litters], [ruddy] like the upper sides of ripening clusters of dates, smooth.

[They are disobedient therein to Ma'add, and fortify themselves therein, since faith has become a faith not to be depended on.]

poems.title: Ode LXXI: Carry this message to thy home
poems.author: Bishr ibn 'Amr
poems.text:
Carry this message to thy home, to Wa'il father of Khulaid — ' Verily I have seen to-day a sight that made me marvel —

' How that the Son of Ja'dah has driven [his camels] far away to al-Buwain, while the Sons of Khafajah are busy following the tracks of a fox.

' And in sooth I see a tribe there other than them, belonging to the folk that inhabit al-Amil, the rich in herbage.

['And I felt disgust at what I saw, and it revolted me; and I had been angry, if I had seen any advantage in anger.']

I humbled not myself through fear among them, and when they drank, I was invited to drink with them ;

And when they played at their appointed times for play, I did not with-draw myself to pass the night apart, but played with them.

And all night long a skilled songstress sang antiphonally with another like her, young and fair, brought up in luxury, and struck the resounding lute,

Among brothers who join together generous heart and hand, who break up their possessions [to give them away] when the bite of Winter nips men sorely.

Thou seest the best of their raiment full of holes : but their Mashrafite swords they dress up in gold brocade.

'Amr son of Marthad is the noble in all his doings : and his sons — he was the generous, and he begat generous seed.
